body:
## What changed

Typing into the playback command palette no longer fires the playback keys behind it: `LoadingShell`'s key handler now lives inside `ShellFrame`, where the existing command-mode context can actually tell it the palette is open.

## Details

**The bug.** During playback, press `/` and type a command name. Each letter also ran its playback key: `q` stopped playback, and `n`, `p`, `a`, `u` skipped, rewound, or toggled autoplay and autoskip. Typing `quit` ended the stream before the command ran.

**The cause.** `LoadingShell` guarded its `useInput` handler with `useShellCommandModeOpen()`, but that context is provided by `ShellFrame` to its children only. `LoadingShell` renders `ShellFrame`, so it sits above the provider and always read the default `false`; the `if (commandModeOpen) return;` guard could never fire. Nothing tested it.

**The fix.** The handler moves, unchanged, into a small `PlaybackShellInput` component rendered inside the frame. No new prop, no new state, and `ShellFrame` is untouched. The same guard also sits in front of the Escape-to-cancel branch, so Escape on a cancellable surface (resolving) should now close the palette instead of cancelling the resolve. The new test does not cover that path.

**Scope check.** `LoadingShell` is the only shell that passes `letterKeysHandledExternally`, and it is the root of the playing surface (`playback-mount-shell.tsx`, a separate return branch from that file's own `ShellFrame`), so no outer provider hides this at runtime. I found it by recording the real demo harness: typing `/` then `quit` with no Enter sent the app to post-play.

## Verification evidence

Tested commit `c1caa4573`. Run on this branch alone, directly, not from a turbo cache replay.

| Command | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| typecheck: `packages/design`, `packages/providers`, `apps/cli` | clean |
| `bun run lint` (all workspaces) | 0 errors; CLI 20 warnings, same as `main` |
| `bun run fmt:root:check`, `bun run --cwd apps/cli fmt:check` | clean |
| `bun run lint:anti-slop:baseline` | passes, 4,414 findings, no rule above baseline |
| `bun run verify:doc-paths` | clean |
| `bun run --cwd apps/cli test` (unit) | 5,790 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail |
| `bun run --cwd apps/cli test` (integration) | 295 pass, 25 skip, 0 fail |
| `bun run --cwd packages/providers test`, `apps/docs test` | 901 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; 288 pass / 0 fail |
| `bun run guard` | passed (ran via the pre-commit hook on the changeset) |
| `bun run build` | passes (10 tasks) |

**Regression test.** `loading-shell-command-mode.test.tsx` mounts `LoadingShell` in the playing state and sends one chunk per keystroke, as a terminal does (a multi-character chunk is a paste to Ink and would hide the bug). Confirmed by putting `origin/main`'s `LoadingShell` back on a clean tree: 2 of 3 tests fail, and the control passes.

- Typing `quitnpau` into the open palette fires `stop, autoskip, next, previous, autoplay, autoskip`.
- A key typed before Escape still stops playback, so closing the palette is covered too.

The Escape test waits 60 ms inside `act`, because Ink defers a lone ESC to tell it apart from an escape sequence. `calendar-route-lifecycle.test.tsx` uses the same idiom for the same reason.

**Not exercised:** a real playback session with mpv (the test and the harness use the real `LoadingShell` and `ShellFrame`, not the full app); macOS and Windows (left to CI); the installer suites (the 25 integration skips include the pwsh-gated ones); live provider and Discord smokes; `verify:doc-coverage` (hosted-only).

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`bun run changeset`) — required for user-facing CLI changes; N/A for docs-only or non-release infra
- [x] `bun run guard` passes when `apps/cli/package.json`, changelogs, or `.changeset/**` changed
- [x] `bun run fmt && bun run lint && bun run test && bun run typecheck` passes locally
- [x] `bun run build` passes for feature, playback, provider, release, or packaging-sensitive changes
- [x] Live provider or Discord smokes were skipped intentionally: no provider or Discord code changed
title: fix(app-shell): let the playback command palette own the keyboard
